tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "Hi, I forgot my password and the reset email never arrived. Can you help?" Write the reply an agent would send.

tasks.expectation: Acknowledges the order number, states the 3-5 business day refund window, and tells the customer what to do if it does not appear by day 5 (contact support again / escalate), without inventing a specific new date.

tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "How do I cancel my monthly subscription?" Write the reply.
tasks.expectation: Gives a concrete, actionable path to cancel (e.g. account settings > subscription > cancel) and states that access continues until the end of the current billing period.

tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "Can you email me a copy of last month's invoice for my accounting team?" Write the reply.
tasks.expectation: Confirms the invoice will be sent or explains exactly where the customer can download it themselves (billing/invoices section), and does not ask for information the company should already have (like the account email).

tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "My order was supposed to arrive yesterday and tracking hasn't updated in 3 days." Write the reply.
tasks.expectation: Apologises for the delay, states a concrete next step (checking with the carrier / offering a replacement or refund if it does not arrive by a stated point), and does not blame the customer.

tasks.expectation: Thanks the customer for the suggestion, states clearly whether this is already available, planned, or will be logged as feedback, and does not promise a specific ship date that was not given.

tasks.expectation: Gives the concrete location of the download (order confirmation email / account > purchases / library) and offers a fallback (resend the link) if the customer still cannot find it.

tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "I was charged twice for my order #77210 on the same day, once for $49.99 and once for $49.99. My bank statement shows both. I need this fixed." Write the reply, including what happens next and roughly when.
tasks.expectation: Acknowledges the duplicate charge as an error to be corrected (not disputed), states that one of the two charges will be refunded, gives a concrete timeframe for the refund to appear, and does NOT ask the customer to dispute it with their bank first.

tasks.expectation: Identifies that this is a fulfillment/shortage issue rather than a lost-package issue, commits to a concrete resolution (ship the missing mirror or refund for it), and asks nothing of the customer that is unreasonable (e.g. does not ask them to prove the box was empty with photos if not necessary).

tasks.task: Draft a support reply to this ticket: "I signed up on the 15th but got charged again on the 1st of next month, only 16 days later, not a full month. Is that right?" tasks.expectation: Correctly explains that billing aligns to the 1st of the calendar month (not to the signup anniversary), that the short first period was a prorated partial month, and that the charge on the 1st is expected and correct — not an error — without contradicting itself.

tasks.expectation: Explicitly acknowledges the conflict between the two stated policies, resolves it in the customer's favor per the given rule (website policy of 30 days governs), states clearly that the return on day 20 is accepted, and does not leave the customer with an ambiguous 'it depends' answer.
